No legacy v1-era APIs (no app.config.ts, vinxi, nitropack, or cache()).

app/package-lock.json:2311 — nitro resolved to 3.0.260903-beta, the Nitro v3 prescribed by the SolidStart v2 deployment-plugins guide

dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: every package is required by the documented v2 setup and each is at its current stable line. Only nitro is a prerelease tag, which is what the framework currently prescribes rather than a misjudgment.

evidence: app/src/lib/queries.ts:3-47 — all server data access funnels through one module of `query` wrappers; components never see the PokeAPI shape
app/src/lib/types.ts:1-61 — typed view models at the client/server boundary, consumed by every component
app/vite.config.ts:1-9 — all framework/deployment config in one 9-line file, matching what `create solid` generates today
app/src/components/Section.tsx:5-8 — a11y section pattern (aria-labelledby + heading id) factored into one component so a landmark change touches one file
app/src/lib/server/pokeapi.ts:130-140 — ingestion casts liberally to `any` (`records.filter(Boolean) as any[]`, `(t: any)`), so an API shape drift surfaces as runtime undefined, not a type error
app/package.json:6-12 — no `typescript` devDependency and no `typecheck` script, so the 66 lines of type annotations are never verified (vite build doesn't typecheck)
churn_resistance.rationale: Data access is isolated behind one module with typed view models, config is in one place, and nothing reaches into framework internals, so a router or Nitro upgrade touches entry files and vite.config only. The main weakness is that the server-side ingestion is untyped `any` and there's no typecheck step to enforce the boundary types.

findings.issue: No `typescript` devDependency or `typecheck` script; `vite build` compiles without type-checking, so the boundary types in `src/lib/types.ts` and the annotations throughout are never verified.
findings.suggestion: Add `typescript` as a devDependency and a `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"` script (plus `"types": ["@solidjs/start/env", "vite/client"]` in tsconfig) so the type boundary actually enforces anything.

findings.issue: Server-side `fetch` calls have no AbortSignal/timeout; a slow or hung API blocks the whole render (mode "async" waits for everything).
findings.suggestion: Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)` to `fetch` and treat timeouts like 404/5xx.

findings.issue: PokeAPI payloads are consumed through `any` (`as any[]`, `(t: any)` in pokemonDetail/moves handling), weakening the otherwise well-typed boundary.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal payload interfaces (species, pokemon, type, move, ability) in `lib/server` and parse into the view models; a data change then fails the typecheck instead of rendering blanks.

findings.issue: `"types": ["vite/client"]` omits `@solidjs/start/env`, which the v2 migration guide prescribes; it's only compensated by the triple-slash reference in app/src/global.d.ts:1.
findings.suggestion: Add `"@solidjs/start/env"` to the tsconfig `types` array as documented.

findings.issue: Nitro is pinned to a prerelease (`^3.0.260903-beta`). It's what SolidStart v2 requires today, but expect a dependency bump when Nitro v3 reaches a stable tag.
findings.suggestion: Keep it (it is prescribed), but treat the nitro major as a tracked upgrade rather than a routine patch.

findings.issue: The `Switch/Match when={x() === null}` not-found pattern is copy-pasted across all five detail routes in addition to the `[...404].tsx` catch-all.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small `<DetailPage data={...}>` wrapper so the 404/title wiring lives in one place.

summary: This is a fully current SolidStart v2 app: vite.config.ts with `solidStart()` + `nitro()`, the `query`/`"use server"`/`createAsync`/`preload` data stack, and a minimal six-dependency manifest with nothing the framework doesn't require. Data access is cleanly isolated behind one server module with typed view models, so framework or API changes stay contained. The remaining risks are the untyped `any`-based ingestion of PokeAPI payloads, no TypeScript tooling to verify the annotations, and server fetches without timeouts.
